bull_bear.body:
- Net Debt to Equity has risen across the shown period: 0.2x (FY22), 0.2x (FY23), 0.3x (FY24), 0.4x (FY25), 0.5x (FY26).
- FY26 cash flow: net cash from operating activities Rs 53.3 Cr against net cash used in investing activities of Rs -54.9 Cr and financing of Rs -7.4 Cr; cash and cash equivalents ended FY26 at Rs 2.0 Cr versus Rs 11.0 Cr a year earlier.
- Balance sheet at Mar-26: Shareholders' Funds Rs 346.5 Cr, LT Borrowings Rs 43.2 Cr, ST Borrowings Rs 141.3 Cr, Capital WIP Rs 38.3 Cr.
- Shareholding as on 30-June-26: Promoters 74.5%, Public 25.5%; the deck states no dividend or buyback policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- "40 + Years of Expertise: A leader in manufacturing aluminium powders, foils, and conductors/ cables", with products used in explosives, AAC blocks, pesticides and pharmaceuticals, and "a strong presence in the domestic market and expanding exports to Europe and Africa".
- Segment-wise revenue mix given as Aluminium Powders 62%, Aluminium Foils 26%, Aluminium Conductors 12% — the company-overview slide labels this mix "(FY26)" while the product slides label the same 62%/26%/12% as "Contributes ~X% of Total Revenue (as of Q1FY27)".
- JV with Toyo Aluminium K.K. (Japan) for aluminium paste (Toyal MMP India Pvt Ltd; MMPIL Holding 26.0%, Toyo Holding 74.0%) described as the "First-ever JV by Toyo Aluminum outside Japan", with MMP holding a "Sole Supply arrangement for their main raw material (atomized powders)".
- Associate Star Circlips & Engineering Ltd (MMPIL Holding 26.06%, Promoter Holding 73.94%) is described as the "Largest manufacturer of Circlips, retaining rings and carbon steel fasteners, fine blank parts in India", with 800+ products, OEMs including Tata Motors, Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, TVS, Honda Cars, Renault and Nissan, and exports to Germany, USA and Japan contributing 35-40% of its revenue.
- "Strategic location in Central India with proximity to the manufacturing hub for all the key end user industry segments"; ongoing development with ISRO for advanced aluminium powders.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Fire incident] Q1FY26 "included a one-time exceptional loss arising from the fire incident at the Umred plant"; the deck attributes FY26 ROE/ROCE weakness to "the operational disruption in Q1FY26, which resulted in an estimated revenue loss of Rs 40-50 Cr and PAT impact of Rs 11-12 Cr".
- [Subsidiary ramp-up drag] The deck flags "an EBITDA loss of Rs 1.35 Cr incurred by newly incorporated subsidiaries during their ramp-up phase" and says newly incorporated subsidiaries in the ramp-up phase incurred initial losses in FY26.
- [Group structure] MMP Electricals Pvt. Ltd. (wholly owned subsidiary) houses Polymer Insulators, described as "Recently commissioned and currently in the initial ramp up phase"; MMP Cables Private Limited (wholly owned subsidiary) houses LVPC, Covered Conductor and Wire Rod.
- [End-market drivers cited] Coal production growth "from 1bn tons to 1.50 bn tons till 2030 as per government of India projections"; electricity demand "will grow from 243 GW to 366 GW till 2031-32"; India's anti-dumping duty of "$619-$873/MT" on Chinese aluminium foil (up to 80 microns, excluding <5.5 microns); GST on AAC blocks reduced from 18% to 12%.
- [Filing-date discrepancy] The covering letter's subject line reads "Quarter and Year (Q-1)/FY26-27 ended 31st March, 2027" while its body reads "Quarter and year (Q-1)/FY25-26 ended 31st March, 2026"; the presentation itself is titled Q1FY27.
business.title: Notable from the deck

deepdive.thesis: The deck positions MMP Industries as a 40+ year Nagpur-based aluminium processor claiming "Leadership and Excellence in Aluminium" across powders, foils and conductors/cables, now diversifying into polymer insulators and LT power cables while backward-integrating into aluminium wire rod.
